runes.mechanism: A gift between two sides: something leaves one hand and is received by another, and what arises between them belongs to both and is not counted.
New small life and the care that lets it grow: something fragile begins, and is given room rather than forced.
A word or sound that arrives and changes something: speech heard at the right moment gives a thing its name or its meaning.
Guarding alertness: something watches or stands between a threat and what it protects, open to the world yet letting not everything in.
Value that lives only while it moves: what is used and passed on grows, what is left standing loses its strength.
Time that does the work: what was done long before ripens at its own pace and shows as a result that cannot be hurried.
What is inherited and where one returns: things, ways and places handed down, and the choice of what to carry on.
An uninvited force from outside breaks what looked solid: the plan falls apart, and afterwards it shows what is gone and what held.
The person among people: one sees oneself in or through others, as in a mirror.
A small light that reveals: something that was there all along gets a shape, and once seen it cannot be unseen; a flame that needs feeding.
A direction that costs something: taking one side or keeping one's word and paying the price for it knowingly.
The sharp edge at a threshold: something stops a move just before it is made, and the stop protects or shows what the rush would have missed.
The closed vessel: something exists but is not yet shown or known — not "nothing", but "not yet".
The unmarked: no sign, no name yet — an open space where meaning has not been written.
Standstill: something that was moving has stopped and is held as it is, and in the stillness one thing stays in view.
Ripening inside: from outside nothing seems to happen while something completes itself within, closed until it is ready.
A moment when things fall into place and lighten: shared joy in the middle of things, not a reward for finishing.
Movement made by two: progress that comes only when two find a common rhythm and neither forces the other.
A road made by going: step follows step, a rhythm is found only by moving, and the question is whether the way still leads where one means to go.
The sun's light and strength: it simply shines, and by it one sees where one stands; too bright, it dazzles.
Raw bodily strength that shows only when it is needed: a weight or resistance gives way to a force that was already there.
Holding through change: something bends, stands between two states or endures a long strain, and does not break.
The turn from dark to light: a shift after which the same world looks different and cannot be seen the old way.
Lack and constraint: something is missing or cannot be had, and the pressure shows what is truly needed.
Water and what moves under the surface: something is sensed before it can be explained, or a hidden current finds its own way.

images.image: The umbrella turns inside out in the gust; you push it back and walk on.
Your foot finds the brake as the car ahead drifts, before you know why.
Someone finally says it aloud, and the room is not the same room.
A drop has frozen at the tip of an icicle, just before it falls.
Two people carry a long mirror through the doorway, one pausing as the other turns.
You climb the last flight of stairs on legs that have nothing left.
The phone is at two per cent, and you send the one message that matters.
You turn down the praise and say whose work it was.
One wall in the new flat is bare, and nothing has been decided for it.
Dinner is burnt, and the table laughs over bread and cheese.
The fog lifts, and the marker you had been walking toward is there.
You turn the map on your phone, and the street falls into place.
You bring a dish to the shared dinner and leave with a plate of someone else's cooking.
There is a recording of your own voice, and you cannot recall what it says.
The broken bone knits under the cast, and nothing can be seen of it.
On the long drive you miss your turning because the road was so easy to follow.
The small sums set aside each month have quietly added up to the course fee.
A friend copies the way you tap your foot, and you had never noticed it.
About to post the photo, you notice someone in it who was never asked.
A chain of bubbles rises through the dark water, then stops beneath the clear ice.
Two people walk side by side, and neither could say who set the pace.
The lid holds, and holds, and gives when your whole hand closes on it.
The phone hits the tiles, and the evening is suddenly about something else.
You tell the referee the ball was out, and your own team loses the point.
The form has one box with no label, and you leave it empty.
Halfway through the dishes a song comes on, and you both join in.
The phone is silenced for the night, with three numbers allowed to ring through.
You thread the needle the way you were shown, long ago, without thinking.
The idea comes mid-step, and you stop to catch it before it goes.
A parcel arrives with no sender's name on it.
The dough rests under a tea towel, and by morning it has doubled.
The path across the grass is on no plan; it is where everyone actually walks.
After months of practice, you answer in the new language without translating first.
In a friend's story of that evening you appear as someone you had not met.
The words are in your mouth, and you hold them until the other person has finished.
The waterfall has become a wall of ice, its last streams held against the rock.
The seedling droops for a week in its new pot, then puts out one leaf.
The chain rusts on the bicycle that stays in the shed.
A power cut ends the video call and takes the unsaved slide with it.
Everyone agreed in the corridor; on the form there is one name, and it is yours.
A new document is open, and the first line is still yours to choose.
Someone has remembered how you take your coffee.
You answer the unknown number, and give your name only after they give theirs.
The table has moved through three homes and still stands in the kitchen.
The new bulb in the hallway shows a crack that was always in the ceiling.
The runner slows to a walk on the hill and does not stop.
You turn back at the door, sure something is left behind, before you know what.
One sentence in the voice message, and the day has a different shape.
The tree planted as a sapling beside the bench now shades the place where you sit.
You hear your own phrase come out of a friend's mouth and learn how it sounds.
The reply is written in a single breath, and your thumb stops above send.
The water is off for the morning, and one bottle has to do for everything.
The child ties the shoelace wrong, and your hands stay where they are.
The battery you never use is flat on the day you need it.
The flight is cancelled at the gate, and the whole day has to be planned again.
The curtains open, and the colour you chose by lamplight is another colour.
At dawn the street that was strange in the dark is the one you know.
One has brought the coffee, the other has saved the seat, and neither keeps count.
The door opens on its chain, just far enough to see who is knocking.
The recipe card is in another hand, with one change added in yours.
The phone light finds the dropped key, and beside it the earring given up for lost.
The tall grass lies flat in the wind and is standing again by evening.
Your voice drops when your friend goes quiet, before either of you knows why.
Said aloud, the plan sounds different from the one in your head.
The lift stops between floors, and the building goes on humming around it.
Two people share a long saw, and the blade runs clean when each pulls in turn.
The stuck window gives when you lean into the frame with both hands.
One seat is left on the last bus, and you see at once who needs it.
The child struggles with the zip, and you wait while they try again.
The candle kept for a special evening has never been lit.
The cake leans to one side, and no one at the table minds.
The cloud lifts, and you see how far up the slope you already are.
You read the same message again in the morning, and it says something else.
The last piece on the plate is cut in two without a word.
The message says the result is ready, but not yet what it is.
After days of rehearsing alone, the first sentence of the speech comes out whole.
A few lengths in, the strokes find a rhythm that no longer needs counting.
